subject: Clarify slab concessions and dashboard scope for observability add-on
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya@kindredhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-on pricing — retention, tracing & dashboards

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked the runtime performance and the dashboard UX. Before we move to procurement, finance wants a clear picture of the add-on economics for observability: specifically retention (hot storage + archival), distributed tracing (ingest and trace retention), and the advanced dashboards pack (seats and per-query pricing).

Two asks:
- Can you confirm list pricing for those three line items and the typical enterprise concessions you offer (slab vs metered, crediting approach for overage)?
- Our procurement has asked for a hypothetical credit/concession if we commit to a 24-month slab for storage (20TB hot + archival profile) and 50 concurrent dashboard seats. What level of concession do you normally extend and what guardrails do you require?

If you can send a short matrix (slab tiers + example concessions) and an initial SOW-level estimate we can loop procurement. Targeting an internal review this week.

Best,
Anya
Director, Platform & Data Engineering
Kindred Health

Attachments: none
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@kindredhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing — retention, tracing & dashboards

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear list of asks and for the time last week. Short answer up front: we can support both slab and metered paths. I've attached a compact matrix that shows list rates and two concession paths we typically recommend (Conservative: slab + modest credits; Aggressive: term + volume concession + pilot credits).

High-level notes:
- Retention/storage: list slab tiers start at $0.20/GB-month for hot with a separate archival tier at $0.015/GB-month. For a 24-month 20TB hot commit we typically quote a slab discount and offer upfront credits for the first three months of burst ingestion.
- Tracing: ingest is metered by span volume; we can cap egress and offer a discounted retention taper after month 12 for long tail traces.
- Dashboards pack: priced as seat + per-query guardrail for heavy aggregation widgets; seats can be bundled to core seats at a discounted pass-through rate.

I'll propose two concrete options in a follow-up once I confirm internal approval for concessions (looping Ben for guidance on maximums). Attached: observability_pricing_v3.pdf and dashboard_feature_matrix.xlsx.

Would you prefer the quote as a slab-first option or as a metered fallback? I can include a pilot credit line if you commit to a 12- or 24-month term.

Cheers,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- observability_pricing_v3.pdf (compact pricing matrix)
- dashboard_feature_matrix.xlsx (feature-by-feature vs our standard dashboards)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Kindred concessions — guidance

Evy — quick internal note before you lock the offer. High-level thoughts:

1) Concession ceiling: for a 24-month, 20TB hot slab + 50 dashboard seats, we can go up to 15% off list on add-on line items (storage+tracing+dashboards) in year 1 if the customer signs an ARR+commit that includes a dedicated Redwood Dedicated capacity commit of >= $250k annual. If no Dedicated commit, cap discount at 10%.

2) Pilot credits: offer 2 weeks of burst credits for ingestion and 10k free dashboard queries during first 60 days (no roll-over). Good sales motion to validate value.

3) Seat bundling: tie advanced dashboard seat discounts to core-seat growth (e.g., 1 advanced seat discounted per 10 core seats) so we protect long-term unit economics.

4) Legal/Procurement asks: procurement often pushes for auto-scaling guardrails and data-retention deletion windows. Ensure SOW calls out retention SLAs and exportability.

Ask: confirm if you want me to approve 12% (conservative) or 15% (aggressive) for this account. If we go 15% I'll need the cross-sell commitment (Dedicated or 12-month minimum core API commit).

Ben
VP, Revenue — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observability add-on pricing — retention, tracing & dashboards

Anya — appreciate the quick turnaround on timelines. Based on internal guidance, here are two concrete options; attached is a draft SOW (KND-4092-MAP-v1.docx) and the pricing matrix.

Option A — Slab-First (recommended if you want predictable unit economics)
- 24-month commitment: 20TB hot + standard archival profile
- List slab rate: $0.20/GB-month hot -> Effective after 15% concession: $0.17/GB-month
- Archival: $0.015/GB-month (no concession applied to archival below $50/mo bucket)
- Tracing: 12% off list for span ingest + tiered retention taper after month 12
- Dashboards: 50 advanced seats at $45/seat/month list -> 12% concession -> $39.60/seat/month; includes 10k free queries/month for first 2 months
- Pilot credits: 48 hours of ingestion burst credits + 10k dashboard queries during onboarding
- Conditions: 24-month SOW signed; commit to an annual core API spend >= $250k to unlock 15% instead of 12% on all add-ons.

Option B — Metered-first (recommended if usage is uncertain)
- No slab commit; metered storage bill at list rates with monthly invoice
- Tracing: standard metering, first 100k spans free for first 30 days
- Dashboards: seat pricing at list; 4-week trial (10k queries) included
- Concession path: can convert to slab within 90 days with retroactive crediting for pilot usage (up to 25% of pilot consumption)

Next steps
- If Option A is acceptable, I'll send a redlined SOW and a DocuSign link; we ask that concessions be accepted within 14 days to hold pricing.
- If you prefer Option B, I can provide a month-by-month forecast template.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to walk procurement through the guardrails if helpful.

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
